implementation_notes: The Swift standard library gives Result<Success, Failure> with exactly one failure value, so accumulation must be hand-written: a small value type with an errors array, a mutating add method and a hasErrors predicate, returned from the validation function. Passing it as inout reads closer to the classic form but makes call sites noisier; returning the struct keeps the check functions pure. Vapor's Validatable/Validations is the framework form for server-side request validation.
pitfalls: A Notification held in a shared class property lets concurrent requests append into each other's diagnostics; return a value or pass it as inout.
Swift's try/? propagation is fail-fast and Error existentials carry no list, so a thrown error is the wrong container for accumulated validation results.
The entries need Codable conformance before they can be returned in an API response, and their strings must not be built from unescaped input.

variants.name: Vapor Validatable/Validations
variants.implementation_notes: Vapor's validation API is the framework realization: conform the content type to Validatable, add rules in the static validations(_:) method, and call validate(content:) before decoding - its documentation states that Codable stops at the first decoding error while the Validation API reports all failures in a single request, exactly the symptom this pattern addresses. Choose it inside Vapor services and keep the manual struct for code outside the framework.
pitfalls: Validation runs before decoding, so the rules read raw values (String, Int); an optional key needs required: false or the check fails on absence.
A failure throws ValidationsError with the collected reasons rather than returning them - catch it at the route level to shape the response.
The default AbortError description joins the reasons into one string, so field-level mapping needs the underlying reasons rather than the message.
